verdict.rationale: Gmail's API documents OAuth scopes and tells developers to pick the narrowest one, so an agent can be granted scoped access such as read-only. Community reports say the scopes are coarse: full control, read, everything except delete, or drafts. No scope can limit access to a specific label or folder, which caps how far least-privilege can go. Missing for 10: label- or folder-level scoping, finer-grained per-agent credential issuance, independent hands-on corroboration of an agent-credential workflow.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Whenever possible, use non-sensitive scopes to narrow access to only the specific features needed by an app.
The Gmail IMAP, POP, and SMTP servers support authorization with the industry-standard OAuth 2.0 protocol.
Gmail API auth scopes already allow read-only access, but one user wants to restrict apps to a specific label or subfolder for better security without forwarding mail.
Gmail API scopes only allow full control, read everything, everything except delete, or drafts.
